splitProposalChirho.criteriaChirho: Applied to material objects and persons: new house, new ropes, new cart, new king, new garments, new grain, newly married man. Focus on temporal novelty and physical freshness.

Applied to divine acts and covenant realities: new covenant (Jer 31:31), new song of praise (Ps 33:3; 96:1; 149:1; Isa 42:10), new things God declares (Isa 42:9; 48:6), new heart and spirit (Ezek 11:19; 18:31; 36:26), new mercies (Lam 3:23). Focus on qualitative transformation and eschatological renewal.

reasoningChirho: The description explicitly contrasts 'physical objects' with 'theological realities of supreme importance' — new covenant, new song, new heart. Physical newness (temporal, material) vs. eschatological/qualitative renewal represents genuinely distinct semantic domains. The new covenant is not merely recently made but qualitatively transformative; the new song is not just composed recently but expresses redemptive worship. This split aligns with the concrete vs. abstract criterion in the instructions.
